>
> For a 4-way cross, the mother and father are assumed to have genotypes AB and CD, respectively. messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Cross type for combined RILs and BC population
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Cross type for combined RILs and BC population
messages.body_plain:
R/qtl doesn't include a cross type for the cross of RILs to one of the parents, nor a way to combine the two crosses.

But in one sense, I think you could think about such data as multiple phenotypes on the one RIL population. In the RIL x parent backcross population, just the RIL chromosome is varying genetically.

karl

messages.subject: logit-scale alphas
messages.body_plain:
Karl

I'm getting some inflated additive effect estimates from a logistic regression model.

I've calculated the odds ratios manually using disease scores and marker genotypes at the peak markers for two QTL

"fitqtl", using the output from 'refineqtl' as the input to the model, gave me coefficients of around -3.89 for each gene (which corresponds to 0.02 odds) however when I estimate these manually using the markers themselves, I obtain a logit coefficient of -1.39 (or odds around 0.249). Why would these estimates differ so greatly in magnitude?

Thanks-

messages.subject: Re: SNP markers with recombination fraction higher than 0.5
messages.subject_clean: SNP markers with recombination fraction higher than 0.5
messages.body_plain:
I'm also working on an allotetraploid with 48 chromosomes -- the previous researcher in my lab found that SNP inheritance behaves very similarly to a diploid because we use the stacks pipeline and the two subgenomes sort independently in that pipeline. The difficulty is figuring out the inheritance of SSRs to anchor your linkage map but can be done -- frequently as is my case we assign the wrong alleles and they need to be switched What I'm having trouble with right now is there are so many linkage groups that I can't visualize any of my plots without half of them getting crowded out. So I don't know which alleles I need to switch or which linkage groups I need to collapse together.

If anyone has any suggestions I'd greatly appreciate it!

On Friday, November 9, 2018 at 7:57:01 PM UTC-5, Fers wrote:
> Hi there,
> I am trying to create a linkage map with data from allotetraploid crop. I have 90 individuals and ~2.5 K SNPs after the QC applied following the KW. Broman manual.
>
> Based on the graph of LOD scores vs rf (gotten with the code below)I can see there are many pairs of markers with rf > 1/2 (0.5 to ~0.8). The LOD scores for those pair of markers are lower than 5.
>
> plot(as.numeric(rf), as.numeric(lod), xlab = "Recombination fraction", ylab = "LOD score"
>
> I have tried to identify those strange markers with the function checkAlleles but the output says is "No apparent problems".
>
> In addition by plotting the estimates of rf (gotten with the code below) I can see there is only one linkage group instead of 26.
>
> lg <- formLinkageGroups(goshir, max.rf = 0.35, min.lod = 6)
> plotRF(goshir, alternate.chrid = TRUE)
>
> Any feedback or idea about this issue in my data will be greatly appreciate it.
>
> Fers

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] logit-scale alphas
messages.body_plain:
In order to comment on the differences you're seeing, I also need to see the code and results from logistic regression.

Are the two sets of coefficient estimates off by a factor of 2? It might have to do with scaling of the predictors to get the standard additive effects in a backcross.

To get the additive effect of a locus, I think fitqtl includes an intercept and takes X = [Pr(AB) - Pr(AA)]/2, equivalent to +1/2 for AB and -1/2 for AA.

karl

Hello,
I have been working through the mqm tutorial for the R/qtl package and was wondering if anyone could clarify the use of 'cofactors'?
I understand that they are genetic markers (or QTL) and treated as covariates, but what is the benefit to using cofactors instead of not using them? Does including cofactors allow you to detect QTL that would otherwise be undetected?

Thanks for the help!

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cofactors in mqm
messages.body_plain:
I don't understand what you mean about phase information. R/qtl is assuming that, for an F2 cross with genotypes A/H/B, that the parents were fully inbred, and so that haplotype in the F1 can't be determined.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cofactors in mqm
messages.body_plain:
That makes sense for an F2, but we have incompletely inbred lines. Therefore, we are restricting our dataset to bi-allelic SNPs (most are biallelic anyway) when using the F2 cross input.

So, can we use phase information from our linkage mapping results (1s and 0s for each marker)?  If coding for an f2 cross can not reflect phase then how would one use phase information for e.g. a CP population cross? I know the codings are numerous for CP, but how would you input phase with those codings?  In the rQTL manual there are many references to “phase known” crosses or data , which we have, but how to include in rQTL when inputting said data?

Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cofactors in mqm
messages.body_plain:
R/qtl includes a "phase-known four-way cross" as a cross type, "4way". It's assuming a cross between four inbreds (AxB)x(CxD).
Coding of genotypes is rather complicated and is described in the help file to read.cross.

karl
